newsitem.title: USA: FBI finds gold mine in Rhode Island backyard.
newsitem.headline: FBI finds gold mine in Rhode Island backyard.

text.p: Federal prosecutors and the FBI announced Tuesday they had struck gold in the backyard of a Rhode Island home owned by the relative of a drug convict.
"We take depositions and ask questions under oath. Sometimes we strike out and sometimes we strike gold," U.S. Attorney for Rhode Island Sheldon Whitehouse told reporters.

Using metal detectors and ground-penetrating radar FBI agents found 82 bars of gold and seven bags of gold pellets weighing nearly 6,000 Troy ounces buried behind a Cranston, R.I. home. Prosecutors put the value of the cache at about $2.1 million.

The house belongs to a relative of Stephen Saccoccia, who is serving 660 years in federal prison for racketeering and money laundering, prosecutors said. Saccoccia was convicted in 1993 for laundering millions of dollars of Colombian cocaine proceeds. His wife, Donna, and 10 others were also convicted.

Cash linked to Colombian drug cartels was picked up from couriers in New York and shipped to precious metals companies in Rhode Island that Saccoccia owned, prosecutors said. The money was later wired to Colombia and Saccoccia kept a percentage of the laundered funds as his fee.

In addition to the prison sentence, he was fined $15.79 million and ordered to forfeit $136,344,231 for racketeering. Whitehouse was seeking to have the $2.1 million in gold forfeited as partial payment.
